title: Best Anden Dehumidifier (2026): A70, A130 & A320 Compared
h1: The Best Anden Dehumidifiers for Grow Rooms
dek: Every gallon you water comes back out of the leaves. Anden builds industrial dehumidifiers sized for exactly that job.
description: The best Anden dehumidifier for your grow: the A70, A130 and 320-pint A320 compared, plus grow-room sizing, 240V wiring and AlorAir alternatives.
intro: An **Anden dehumidifier** is built for one of the toughest moisture loads indoors: a room full of thirsty plants. Anden is the indoor-agriculture brand of Research Products Corporation, the Madison, Wisconsin, company behind Aprilaire, and its grow-optimized industrial dehumidifiers are a common sight in licensed cultivation rooms and serious home grows.

The lineup is straightforward. The **A70**, **A130** and **A320** are named for the pints of water each removes per day at standard 80°F, 60% humidity conditions, so the model number tells you the size. The trick is picking the right one — and deciding whether a single big unit or several smaller ones suits your space better. Below we compare the main Anden models, show how to size one from your watering schedule, see how Anden stacks up against Quest, and point to alternatives from AlorAir.
topPicksLead: For most single grow rooms, the **Anden A130** is the best Anden dehumidifier: it runs on a standard 120-volt circuit while handling the moisture from a substantial canopy.

products.name: Anden A130 Grow-Optimized Industrial Dehumidifier (130 Pints/Day)
cons: Needs a drain or condensate pump
Too much machine for a single tent
products.whyWeLoveIt: The A130 hits the sweet spot for a dedicated grow room: enough capacity for a meaningful canopy without needing a 240-volt circuit. Its compact cabinet can sit on the floor, ride on a shelf or be ducted, which makes it flexible in rooms where floor space is precious.
products.performance: Anden rates it at 130 pints a day at 80°F and 60% relative humidity. Like every dehumidifier, it removes less as the room gets drier and cooler, so a room held at 45% in late flower will see less than the label number. Owners commonly run two A130s rather than one larger unit for redundancy — if one fails, the room isn't left unprotected overnight.
products.notes: Plan drainage first: a gravity line to a floor drain, or a condensate pump if the unit sits below the drain point.

products.name: Anden A70 Grow-Optimized Industrial Dehumidifier (70 Pints/Day)
pros: Industrial build in a small package
Easy to add a second unit later
products.whyWeLoveIt: Consumer dehumidifiers often die young running nonstop in a hot, humid grow room. The A70 brings Anden's commercial-duty build to small rooms and multi-tent setups that don't need 130 pints of capacity.
products.performance: Anden rates it at 70 pints a day at 80°F and 60% humidity. That suits a small room or a couple of tents watered with up to roughly a few gallons a day. If your canopy grows, adding a second A70 is often easier than replacing it with a bigger unit. For a single tent, see our [best dehumidifier for grow tent](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-grow-tent/) picks instead.

products.name: Anden A320 Grow-Optimized Industrial Dehumidifier (320 Pints/Day, 240V)
pros: Replaces two or three smaller units
Designed for ducted or ceiling-area installs
cons: One large unit means less redundancy
products.whyWeLoveIt: Large flowering rooms can transpire dozens of gallons a day. The A320 is Anden's workhorse for those spaces: one machine with the capacity of several smaller ones, taking up less floor space and fewer outlets.
products.performance: Anden rates it at 320 pints a day at 80°F and 60% humidity on a 240-volt supply, so budget for an electrician if your room lacks a dedicated circuit. Many commercial growers pair a big unit like this with a smaller one so humidity stays in check during maintenance. See how it compares with other high-capacity machines in our [best commercial dehumidifier](/best/best-commercial-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.name: AlorAir Storm Elite LGR Dehumidifier

Bulky to place in a tight room
products.whyWeLoveIt: If you want capacity in the same range as the A130 but with a pump built in, the Storm Elite is the one to compare. It's a low-grain refrigerant (LGR) machine from the restoration world, so it's designed to keep pulling water around the clock and to keep going as the air gets drier.
products.performance: AlorAir rates it at 125 pints a day at AHAM conditions and 270 at saturation, with coverage up to 3,000 square feet. Auto-defrost and a filtered intake make it comfortable when a room cools down after lights-off, and the built-in pump lets you send water to a sink or drain without planning a gravity run. Check the spec sheet for amp draw before you plan your circuits. Our [best LGR dehumidifier](/best/best-lgr-dehumidifier/) guide compares it with other LGR units.

products.name: AlorAir Sentinel HDi90 Dehumidifier

products.whyWeLoveIt: If budget matters more than a grow-specific badge, the HDi90 covers much of the A70-to-A130 range for less. It's built for crawl spaces and basements, so it's comfortable running continuously in demanding conditions.
products.performance: AlorAir rates it at 90 pints a day under AHAM conditions and 198 at saturation, for spaces of roughly 2,600 square feet, with defrost operation down to about 33.8°F. In a hot, humid grow room it'll run hard, so keep the filter clean. More models are in our [best AlorAir dehumidifier](/best/best-alorair-dehumidifier/) guide.

items.label: Share of the water plants take up that they release back into the air
Moisture load from every gallon of water you give your plants
Conditions behind Anden's pints-per-day model numbers

blocks.text: That first number is why grow rooms need so much dehumidification. Plants keep only a tiny fraction of the water they drink; nearly all of it leaves through the leaves. If you water 10 gallons a day, roughly 80 pints of moisture will end up in the room's air.

We don't run a lab. We compared Anden's published capacity ratings, electrical requirements and installation guides, checked them against rivals from Quest and AlorAir, and read reviews and grower forum discussions for recurring issues such as drain clogs, coil icing in cooler lights-off periods and early failures.
We focused on the A70, A130 and A320 because their ratings are widely published and they cover most room sizes. Anden also sells other sizes; the sizing method below works for any of them.

sections.heading: What to look for in an Anden dehumidifier

items.label: Capacity matched to your watering
items.text: Multiply the gallons you water per day by eight to get pints of moisture, then choose a unit — or combination — rated above that.

items.label: The right voltage
items.text: The A70 and A130 run on 120V; the A320 needs a 240V circuit. Check your panel before you buy.

items.label: Drainage you can count on
items.text: Industrial units have no bucket. Plan a gravity drain or a condensate pump; see our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide for how pumps work.

items.label: Redundancy
items.text: Two smaller units often beat one large one, because a single failure won't leave the room unprotected during flower.

items.label: Room for the heat
items.text: Every dehumidifier adds heat. In a sealed room, factor that into your air-conditioning load.
sub: Lights-on: heat from lights plus the dehumidifier
Lights-off: humidity spikes as temperatures drop

sections.heading: Which Anden size do you need?

blocks.text: Start with your watering, not your square footage. A small room packed with mature plants can put out far more moisture than a large, sparsely planted one. Use your peak watering day in late veg or flower.

head: Daily watering
Moisture to remove
Anden fit
rows: Multiple A320s or a mix of sizes
blocks.caption: Ratings are at 80°F and 60% humidity. In cooler, drier late-flower rooms, real capacity drops — build in headroom.

blocks.title: Why rated pints aren't the whole story
blocks.text: A dehumidifier pulls the most water from warm, very humid air. Holding a flower room at 45% means each unit removes noticeably less than its label number, so most growers size 20–30% above their calculated load. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) explains how test conditions affect ratings.

sections.heading: Installing an Anden: placement, ducting and drainage

items: **Place it where air moves.** Put the unit where circulation fans carry room air through it, not in a dead corner. Keep the intake and exhaust clear of leaves and walls.

**Consider getting it off the floor.** Anden sells installation accessories, and many growers mount units on shelves or overhead to save floor space. Follow the manual for your model's approved mounting methods.
**Duct if it helps.** Ducting lets the unit sit outside the canopy or serve a room from an adjacent space.
**Run the drain downhill.** Use a gravity line with a steady slope to a floor drain, or install a condensate pump if the drain is higher than the unit.
**Use a dedicated circuit.** Industrial dehumidifiers draw a lot of current. A 240V A320 needs proper wiring by an electrician.
**Control by humidity, not time.** Use the unit's control or a compatible environmental controller with its sensor at canopy height.

blocks.text: For smaller setups, AC Infinity is another grow-focused brand worth a look; see our [best AC Infinity dehumidifier](/best/best-ac-infinity-dehumidifier/) guide. Greenhouse growers should also read our [best dehumidifier for greenhouse](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-greenhouse/) picks, since cold nights change the equation.

For most single grow rooms, the **Anden A130** is the Anden to buy: 130 pints a day on a regular 120V circuit. Choose the **Anden A70** for small rooms and multi-tent setups, and the **Anden A320** for large or commercial rooms with 240V service. If you'd like to compare, the **AlorAir Storm Elite** brings similar capacity with a built-in pump, and the **AlorAir Sentinel HDi90** is the budget route. Size from your watering, add headroom and plan your drain before the unit arrives.

faqs.a: Anden is the indoor-agriculture brand of Research Products Corporation of Madison, Wisconsin — the same company that makes Aprilaire home comfort products.

faqs.q: What size Anden dehumidifier do I need?
faqs.a: Multiply your peak daily watering in gallons by eight to estimate pints of moisture, then add 20–30% headroom. Up to about 40 pints suits an A70; up to about 100 an A130; larger loads an A320 or multiple units.
Yes. The A320 is rated at 320 pints per day and runs on a 240-volt supply, so you'll need an appropriate dedicated circuit. The A70 and A130 run on standard 120V.

faqs.q: Anden A70 vs. A130: which should I buy?
faqs.a: The A70 suits small rooms and a few tents; the A130 suits a full grow room. If you're between sizes, two A70s add redundancy, while one A130 saves space and outlets.

faqs.q: What about the Anden 210 and 710 dehumidifiers?
faqs.a: Anden sells additional sizes beyond the three we cover, and model names follow the same pints-per-day logic. Confirm current capacity, voltage and drainage on the manufacturer's spec sheet, then size them with the watering method above.

faqs.q: Can I use an Anden dehumidifier in a grow tent?
faqs.a: Usually it's better outside the tent, drying the room the tent draws its air from. Industrial units are large for most tents; smaller tents are better served by the picks in our grow tent guide.
